intervals.quote: Then, in the Fall of 1955 at the suggestion and with the moral support of John A. Wheeler, the detector was taken to a new, powerful (700 MW at that time), compact heavy water moderated reactor at the Savannah River Plant in Aiken, South Carolina.

name: Cowan–Reines reactor neutrino experiment
notes: The 1953 attempt at Hanford is the separate experiment:cowan-reines-hanford-1953 (facility:hanford-site), its predecessor: "A tentative identification of the free neutrino was made in an experiment performed at Hanford in 1953" (Science 124, 103), and Reines writes "Our entourage arrived at Hanford in the spring of 1953" (Nobel Lecture).
No collaboration record: a five-author Los Alamos group (Cowan, Reines, Harrison, Kruse, McGuire), not a named collaboration. No detector record is created (not assigned to this stream).

The official SRS timeline lists "Neutrino confirmed at P Reactor" under 1956; the APS plaque page says the definitive experiment was run "in early 1956"; Reines says the detector reached Savannah River in the fall of 1955. These are consistent: installation in fall 1955, running into 1956.
The Savannah River site point is the whole-site centroid; P Reactor itself is not geolocated.

physics_goals.quote: To carry this work to a more definitive conclusion, a second experiment was designed
physics_goals.value: Settle the free-neutrino detection more definitively than the 1953 Hanford experiment, using antineutrino + proton → positron + neutron with a delayed-coincidence signature

summary.plain: In 1955-56 Clyde Cowan and Frederick Reines put a detector beside a reactor at the Savannah River Plant in South Carolina and counted the antineutrinos pouring out of it. Their July 1956 report confirmed the neutrino, the particle Pauli proposed in 1930 and widely thought undetectable.
summary.technical: Delayed-coincidence search for reactor electron antineutrinos through ν̄ + p → e⁺ + n: two water targets of about 200 L loaded with cadmium chloride, between three liquid-scintillator tanks, in an underground room of the P Reactor building 11 m from the reactor centre. 1371 h of running including reactor-off periods; reactor-correlated signal 0.56 ± 0.06 and 2.88 ± 0.22 counts per hour for two selections, with a cross section within 5% of 6.3×10⁻⁴⁴ cm². Follows a tentative 1953 attempt at Hanford.

unique_capabilities.quote: The reaction products were detected as a delayed pulse pair; the first pulse being due to the slowing down and annihilation of the positron and the second to capture of the moderated neutron in cadmium dissolved in the scintillator.
unique_capabilities.value: Delayed-coincidence signature: a positron annihilation pulse followed by a neutron-capture pulse in cadmium dissolved in the scintillator
